sentences.text: This is the second application filed by the applicant under section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No 1056/2022 dated 8.9.2022 registered at police station Jhabua District Jhabua for the offence under section 363, 366, 376, 506 of the Indian Penal Code and section 3/4 of POCSO Act.

As per the prosecution story, on 8.9.2022 while prosecutrix alongwith ladies of her family went to attend a function, at that time at about 12.30 am, applicant forcefully took the prosecutrix in the agricultural field and committed rape upon her.
Accordingly a case has been registered against the applicant.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this matter.
He submits that earlier bail application of applicant was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to renew the prayer after examination of prosecutruix before the trial court.
Prosecutrix has been examined before the trial court and she has turned hostile and not supported the case of prosecution.
Mother and brother of prosecutrix have also been examined and they have also turned hostile.
Final conclusion of trial will take considerable long time.
Hence, he prays that applicant be released on bail.
Per-contra, learned PL for respondent/State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.
Perused the case diary as well as the impugned order of the court below.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by counsel for the parties, nature and gravity of allegation as also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix (PW-1) has been examined before the trail court and she has turned hostile and she categorically stated in her statement that present applicant neither abducted her nor committed any rape upon her, her mother PW-2 & brother PW-3 also deposed in the same manner and final conclusion of trial will take considerable long time, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/-
(Rs. Seventy Five Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by the conditions enumerated u/S. 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE BDJ Sunil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47958942/
